title: Client departure mapping checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a working template for mapping a customer departure ("client left", "did not renew"). Focus is on reconstructing timeline, surfacing evidence, enumerating plausible root causes, and listing concrete counterfactuals and operational actions we could have taken. Designed to tie directly into QBRs and our renewal tracker so PM/CS/Eng can decide runbooks for future accounts.

Usage notes (quick):
- Use after we confirm an account will not renew or when a renewal slips to 30-day churn risk.
- Fill timeline with actual dates; mark evidence items and link tickets/recordings.
- Aim for 30–60 minute working session with AE, CSM, solutions engineer, and an eng owner if technical.
- Keep it messy. This is a Drive working doc; we expect fragments, hypotheses, TODOs.

Template sections (copy for each account):

1) Snapshot header
- Company: <company name>
- ARR / Monthly charge: <amount>
- Contract type: hosted | dedicated | private
- Renewal date: <YYYY-MM-DD>
- STAGE: Non-renewed / Declined / Did not respond / Cancelled early
- Primary owner (CSM): <name>
- AE: <name>
- Support lead or SE: <name>

2) One-line summary (30 words)
- e.g. "Customer decided to consolidate vendors after integration delays and perceived accuracy regressions; pricing not primary driver."

3) Why we lost (hypothesis buckets) — high-level categories (tick as applicable)
- Product fit / accuracy / quality concerns
- Integration or onboarding friction
- Operational costs (latency, tokens, rate limits)
- Pricing / procurement / license constraints
- Compliance / privacy / hosting requirements unmet
- SLA / reliability incidents or trust erosion
- Competitive switch (vendor X offered feature Y)
- Organizational change / budget reallocation at customer
- Sales/process mismatch (expectation vs reality)

4) Timeline (chronological, include owners and evidence links)
- T-180: initial discovery call — owner: AE — notes: <link/summary>
- T-120: POC started — owner: SE — notes: dataset sizes, throughput goals, expected p99 latency <link>
- T-90: First accuracy evaluation report shared — owner: CSM — evidence: drive/folder link, sample output
- T-60: Integration blocker reported (auth / cert issue) — ticket: JIRA-CS-6723 — owner: infra eng — status: unresolved at T-30
- T-40: Pricing negotiation began — owner: AE — notes: discount requested 25%
- T-20: Outage or critical bug surfaced — incident: INC-3334 — SLA breach reported to customer
- T-10: Renewal discussion — customer signals intent to review vendors
- T-0: Non-renewal confirmed — communication: email from contact (copy/paste block)

Notes: include links to call recordings, Slack threads, GitHub issues, incident reports. If missing, note as TODO.

5) Evidence inventory (attach or link; mark confidence)
- Call recordings: <link> — confidence: high/medium/low
- Internal notes / Slack: <link> — relevant quotes
- Support tickets: list keys (INC-xxx, JIRA-xxx)
- Demo artifacts / sample outputs (POC folder)
- Billing/invoice history (billing@sales)

6) Root cause analysis (brief bullets, avoid blame)
- Cause A (technical): e.g., "Indexed tokenizer mismatch caused repeated hallucination in summarization microservice" — evidence: eval-2025-06-10.csv — severity: medium — probable? yes/no
- Cause B (process): "Onboarding SOW timeline slipped 6 weeks due to unclear SE ownership" — evidence: timeline notes — severity: high
- Cause C (commercial): "Procurement required FedRAMP-style docs we couldn't provide in time" — evidence: email thread with procurement

7) Counterfactuals (if we had done X, customer likely to have renewed)
- CF-1: Faster SE assignment and dedicated weekly cadence in first two weeks of POC — expected impact: reduce time-to-value by 30%
- CF-2: Provide pre-approved procurement packet and security questionnaire within 5 business days — expected impact: remove procurement blocker
- CF-3: Canary fallback model with lower cost/high-recall configuration to match budget constraints — expected impact: meet throughput SLA at lower unit cost

8) Concrete runbook actions (who does what, by when) — prioritize by effort/impact
- Short-term (0–14 days):
  - Reach out to buyer for debrief and permission to run post-mortem (owner: CSM)
  - Open an internal RCA ticket and link this doc (owner: CSM)
- Mid-term (14–60 days):
  - Create procurement pack template for future accounts in same vertical (owner: GTM Ops)
  - Engineering: create onboarding checklist templates and reduce manual SE steps (owner: solutions-eng)
- Long-term (60+ days):
  - Platform: add a "lightweight hosted variant" pricing tier for budget-sensitive POCs (owner: Product)

9) Renewal tracker integration notes (how this maps into our CRM/Tracker)
- Update renewal status to "lost" and set loss reason tag: e.g., "procurement-failure", "integration-friction"
- Add CF tags back to QBR template for accounts in same cohort
- Flag similar accounts in tracker with same vertical + ARR > X for outreach with new procurement pack

10) Communication templates (short snips)
- Debrief request to customer (email):
  Subject: Quick debrief request — help us improve
  Body: Hi <name>, sorry to hear you've chosen a different direction. Would you be open to a 20-minute debrief to help our team improve? We want to understand the blockers and what we could have done differently.

- Internal wrap note (to execs/stakeholders):
  Subject: [Wrap] <customer> non-renewal — summary and next steps
  Body: TL;DR + top 3 root causes + next 3 actions + owner assignments

11) Retrospective scoring (calibrate collective judgment) — 1–5 scales as strings
- Onboarding clarity: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5
- Product fit: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5
- Response time to blockers: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5
- Commercial alignment: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5
- Net recommendation: Keep / Improve / Archive

12) Handover to Product/Engineering (what to include in the ticket)
- Short description of the failure mode
- Repro artifacts / data points / sample outputs
- Customer impact metrics (error rate, p99 latency during POC, cost delta)
- Suggested mitigation + estimated effort

13) Follow-up checklist (dates and owners)
- T+7: Did we get debrief from customer? Owner: CSM — action: yes/no + notes
- T+14: Internal RCA ticket created and prioritized? Owner: CSM/CS Ops
- T+30: Any product/ops tasks scoped? Owner: Eng Manager

14) Notes to self / loose threads (quick bullet style)
- We should correlate churn reasons with model families (opensourcing vs closed) — add to quarterly analysis
- Possible quick-win: procurement pack + FedRAMP FAQ one-pager
- Ask finance to anonymize billing cases where churn linked to overage spikes

Open questions / TODOs:
- Was the outage on T-20 caused by our runtime or by customer infra? (confirm with SRE)
- Can we surface a "procurement readiness" checkbox in new account intake? (owner: CS Ops)

Appendix: example snippets
- Copy/paste of customer's non-renewal email (redact PII)
- Short list of similar churn cases last 12 months (IDs): CS-201, CS-305, CS-499

Quick checklist (one-line) before closing doc:
- [ ] Internal RCA ticket open
- [ ] Debrief request sent to customer
- [ ] Linked evidence uploaded
- [ ] Renewal tracker updated with loss reason and CF tags
- [ ] Exec wrap note prepared

End of template.

-- informal notes --
I kept this intentionally terse. For small accounts we can do a 1-pager; for strategic we expand timeline and attach full eval artifacts. Use this as the standard we iterate on in CS ops reviews.
